correctness.rationale: All finite-stage skeletons have exactly one unresolved congruence class H_r modulo 3^r, and index reflection i -> 2H_r-i exchanges the two fixed digit values while preserving unresolved positions. Every factor has a fully assigned occurrence by shifting at most one unresolved position to a matching filled copy. A complete first-level three-residue window decomposition produces 16 exact length-eight factors in one of two complementary orientations, with no internal complementary pair; short-factor counts follow by taking prefixes. Factoriality extends the length-eight obstruction, and antimorphic closure equates complement and reversal co-occurrence. All six admissible patterns, all directives, both exceptional fillings, and all lengths are covered. The standalone verifier independently checks 1,296 directive prefixes, 111,150 finite-skeleton residue identities, and the exact overlap table; these are supporting checks, not a replacement for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new theorem proves a same-language antimorphic closure and complete co-occurrence spectra for arbitrary Stewart directives. Fici–Shallit give ordinary-palindrome and factor-complexity theorems, not a reverse-complement closure or exact complementary/reversal factor-pair spectrum. Currie and coauthors establish existence/repetition thresholds for complement-avoiding classes rather than this uniform Stewart classification. Prior records queried semantically and compared by implications; no identified result implies the combined claim. Residual risk from less accessible early choral-sequence papers remains.
residual_risks: Early papers on Stewart choral and generalized choral sequences (e.g. Noche 2008/2011, cited by Fici–Shallit) were not fully inspected and might contain equivalent observations.
Search and semantic database retrieval are not completeness proofs; a similarly phrased Toeplitz antimorphism theorem may exist without the focal terminology.
The present contribution is the three-part symmetry classification, not the previously established complexity 2n or ordinary palindrome list.

value.rationale: The known all-directive Stewart family has factor complexity 2n and a bounded ordinary-palindrome spectrum. A new structural phenomenon emerges: the whole infinite factor language is invariant under a reverse-complement antimorphism, while both ordinary reversal and complement co-occurrence vanish abruptly at the sharp length-eight boundary. The theorem fully classifies both overlap spectra and identifies the underlying 3-adic reflection for every directive, rather than offering a routine isolated count. This informs the exact symmetry action on factors and the relationship between Toeplitz geometry and binary complement-avoidance, independently of general or downstream applications.
